programme: EPAS1 (HIF-2α) with its dedicated antagonist/paralog HIF3A form the core of a hypoxia-response axis; GATA2 and HEY1 sit downstream as the endothelial/Notch-VEGFR2(KDR) effectors that convert HIF2A activity into vascular remodeling and angiogenic sprouting, with NR4A3 contributing the vascular-adhesion/inflammatory arm (VCAM1, ICAM1) typical of activated hypoxic endothelium.
role_in_a: In COPD, sustained alveolar and pulmonary-vascular hypoxia stabilizes EPAS1/HIF-2α in vascular and macrophage compartments, driving pulmonary vascular remodeling (PMID 42397467) and macrophage-intrinsic inflammatory/metabolic reprogramming via GATA2 (PMID 41712459, 39379099); HEY1 is pulled into the same hypoxic circuit as a direct Notch target that falls with hypoxia alongside NOTCH3 in airway epithelium (PMID 33015064), while HIF3A acts as a protective counter-arm limiting alveolar epithelial ferroptosis under the same hypoxic stress (PMID 39310101).
role_in_b: In clear cell renal carcinoma, VHL loss constitutively stabilizes EPAS1/HIF-2α, which is the textbook oncogenic driver of the tumor's angiogenic transcriptional programme (PMID 41714613, 35267567); GATA2, HEY1 and NR4A3 all score highly in the Open Targets ccRCC association (0.96, 0.90, 0.92 percentile respectively), consistent with a shared HIF-driven angiogenic/endothelial module in the tumor vasculature, though no retrieved paper places them there directly the way it does EPAS1.
shared_axis: Both diseases run on the same HIF-2α-centered angiogenic module, just triggered oppositely: reactively in COPD by chronic tissue hypoxia, and constitutively in ccRCC by VHL loss removing the brake on HIF-2α. The downstream vascular-remodeling machinery (GATA2, HEY1, NR4A3) is reused rather than disease-specific.
reasoning: EPAS1's role is independently and strongly documented in both diseases by name (mechanistic COPD vascular-remodeling review and a direct renal-carcinoma EPAS1-regulatory-circuit paper), which anchors the module; but the extension of that module to GATA2, HEY1 and NR4A3 in ccRCC rests on Open Targets percentile scores and one non-specific cancer review (NR4A3, PMID 25446259) rather than papers placing them in ccRCC directly, so the cross-disease link is reasoned rather than retrieved.
support: PMID 42397467 — direct mechanistic account of EPAS1 in COPD pulmonary vascular remodeling; PMID 42206079 — EPAS1/VEGFA variants modulate COPD susceptibility; PMID 42396188 — HIF-2α/MMP12 axis drives emphysema in alveolar macrophages; PMID 41714613 — HIF sustains an EPAS1 transcriptional circuit in clear cell renal carcinoma; PMID 35267567 — HIF-2α as a therapeutic target in solid tumors including ccRCC; PMID 38612943 — EPAS1 flagged in ccRCC drug-discovery screen; PMID 39310101 — HIF3A protects against COPD via inhibiting alveolar ferroptosis; PMID 34953943 — HIF3A-linked lncRNA in cigarette-smoke airway remodeling; PMID 41712459 — GATA2 controls alveolar macrophage inflammatory/metabolic function in COPD; PMID 39379099 — GATA2 downregulation drives pro-inflammatory, phagocytosis-defective pulmonary macrophages; PMID 33015064 — hypoxia directly decreases HEY1 alongside NOTCH3 in airway cells; PMID 28431315 — PM2.5-driven Notch/HEY1 signaling and immune imbalance in COPD; PMID 25446259 — NR4A receptors in oncogene-tumor suppressor networks across cancers generally (not ccRCC-specific).
how_to_falsify: In parallel primary cultures — COPD pulmonary vascular/alveolar macrophage cells under hypoxia, and ccRCC tumor cells with VHL loss — pharmacologically or genetically modulate EPAS1 (e.g. belzutifan or CRISPR knockdown) and measure GATA2, HEY1 and NR4A3 target expression (NOS3, EDN1, KDR, EFNB2, VCAM1, ICAM1) by RNA-seq/ChIP; if these genes fail to move concordantly with EPAS1 activity in both tissue contexts, or ChIP shows EPAS1 does not occupy their loci in either setting, the shared-axis claim is wrong.
caveats: Tissue pairing is kidney vs lung — different vascular beds and cell types, so 'shared module' means shared transcriptional logic, not shared tissue context. 195 patient-group comparisons come from only 4 independent cohort pairs, so the count reflects clinical-subgroup splits within few cohorts, not broad replication. The ccRCC literature record is thin outside EPAS1 and TBX3 per the overall note, and no retrieved paper addresses both diseases or names the shared factors together — the shared_axis is an inference from HIF biology, not a documented finding. TBX3 (119/195) was deliberately left out of the programme despite strong recurrence: its targets (gap junctions, TP53/CDKN2A/CDKN1A, developmental genes) show no thread to the hypoxia/angiogenesis module in the data given, and its COPD/ccRCC evidence (GWAS lung-function signal; cell-death prognostic signature) supports each disease separately, not a shared mechanism. SOX17, TCF4, DOT1L, TFAP2A, BACH2 and KLF10 were excluded from the programme for the same reason — COPD-only evidence with no mechanistic tie to the EPAS1/HIF3A/GATA2/HEY1/NR4A3 axis. Single-view factors (JARID2, NR1H2, HOXA1, NCOA2, PAX4, EP300, ZFPM2, POU2AF1, TFAM, NFKBIB, ZHX3, ZBTB17) were excluded as required and play no role here.
